messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to add a lightweight 'admit smoke' stage in the onboarding pipeline. goal: fail fast on compat and perf regressions before expensive evals.

dan: +1 to fail-fast. what's part of the smoke? tokenizer, kv-cache sanity, and a 1-minute latency/throughput microbench?

maria: Exactly. keep resources tiny: 1 GPU, 1 warmup sequence, then 10 sample requests covering common seq lengths. if any large mem regression or tokenization mismatch -> reject.

jonathan: Tradeoff: more false positives vs catching bad commits early. we should tune thresholds per model family. e.g., quantized 4-bit will have different latency baseline.

ashley: We can keep model-family profiles in a small YAML and compare observed numbers to a tolerance band. If profile missing, mark as "needs manual review" not auto-reject.

kevin: How do we detect tokenizer mismatch reliably? examples?

maria: Steps I have in mind:
- run tokenizer on 50 seed prompts -> check token counts don't differ by >2 tokens on average vs expected.
- load model and run one step with dummy KV to ensure shapes align (no runtime shape errors)
- run microbench script to collect p50/p95 latency and peak memory.

jonathan: Suggest a small script snippet we can add to admit-checks:```
# run quick compat
redwoodctl admit-check --model $MODEL_TAR --tests tokenizer,kvshape,smokebench \
  --smoke-seqs 10 --timeout 60
```

maria: Nice. Also add a best-effort attempt to export ONNX or TFRT metadata so we can catch export-time surprises. optional: if export fails, mark as "needs export-fix".

dan: CI integration? I assume this runs in the model-admit pipeline job and posts a summary. we should avoid flapping on noisy infra.

ci-bot: CI job started: model-admit-smoke/1825567890 for model: llama-rtl-v2 (node: admit-runner-3)

kevin: For perf thresholds, store baseline per model-version hash. how do we get baseline for new family? maybe run an initial long-run offline to seed the baseline.

ashley: Agreed. baseline seed flow: when a model is first added with "seed-baseline" flag, run full benchmark offline (not gate) and store profile. later admits compare to that.

maria: Edge cases: models that use custom ops or require special libs. For those we fallback to manual review and mark pipeline note. we need clear audit log for why something was gated.

jonathan: Also record small artifacts: tokenizer vocab diff, a short perf trace (flamegraph snippet), and the KV-shape dump. store as attachments in the admit record.

kevin: OK. what's the acceptance criteria to roll this to prod?

maria: 1) implement smoke script + redwoodctl flag, 2) CI integration + clear pass/fail semantics, 3) baseline seeding flow + model-family YAML, 4) docs and runbook for manual review.

ashley: I'll take docs and runbook. volunteer to own the "needs manual review" UI text.

jonathan: I'll prototype the smokebench harness and shape-checker. will send PR by EOD Friday.

dan: I'll wire the CI job and make sure we only auto-reject when tests fail deterministically (shape/tokenizer/runtime errors). perf regressions should be warnings by default for first 2 weeks.

maria: timeline sounds good. one more: add a short opt-out label for very experimental models so teams can bypass smoke for iterative dev. must be audited.

ci-bot: CI job completed: model-admit-smoke/1825567890 -> WARNINGS: perf_p95_up 12% (threshold 10%), tokenizer_avg_delta 0.5 tokens. details: /ci/artifacts/1825567890/report.html

maria: Perfect. we'll discuss the warning thresholds next sync. thanks all. :thumbsup:
